title: Walk Through Database Tables Using the 'Database Walkthrough' Slide Reference
summary: Use the OptiSweep Day 2 “Database Walkthrough” segment to compile a table-by-table list of the database tables that are covered, and capture the walkthrough’s stated associations/purpose for each table (only when the table names/purpose are readable in the provided video frames).
when_to_use: When you need to identify which database tables are covered in the OptiSweep Training Day 2 “Database Walkthrough” segment and you have the relevant video frames available to read the table names and any stated purpose/associations.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a live troubleshooting guide for database connectivity or runtime failures (the provided packet does not include a live SSMS/Helix DB workflow or query steps).
Do not use this procedure to infer table names/purpose when the video frames are not readable; stop and request higher-resolution frames or the next segment that shows the specific table names.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Play the Day 2 video segment, capture the table names as they appear, and record the walkthrough’s stated associations/purpose for each table only when visible/readable.

L1_support (reviewer/second pass, if available): Validate that each recorded table name matches what is visible in the captured frames and that the recorded purpose/association is limited to what is readable/said in those frames.
access_or_tools_needed: Training video playback for FORTNA OptiSweep Training Day 2
The 'Database Walkthrough' slide frame as a reference

visual_references.description: Frame with the walkthrough overview of WCS-created databases and the stated table associations/purpose (e.g., EntityLogs used for logging; Audit tracks AGDID/current geek task ID/command GUID; Geek AGV action logging; lattice code model; OPC configuration; OPC tags).

steps.title: Locate the 'Database Walkthrough' slide frame referenced in the Day 2 training segment
steps.purpose: Establish the correct segment reference point for the table-by-table walkthrough.
steps.instruction: Open/play the FORTNA OptiSweep Training Day 2 video and navigate to the “Database Walkthrough” segment where the presenter says “All right, we're gonna walk through all the tables”. Use the captured frame titled “Database Walkthrough” as your reference point.
steps.expected_result: You can identify the “Database Walkthrough” segment reference frame in the video (the frame where the presenter states the walkthrough will cover all tables).
steps.healthy_condition: The video is at/near the timestamped frame where the presenter says “All right, we're gonna walk through all the tables” and the frame OCR indicates “Database Walkthrough”.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot locate the “Database Walkthrough” frame or the table walkthrough does not appear in the expected segment.

actions.label: Find the “Database Walkthrough” frame
actions.exact_action: Locate the frame where the presenter says “All right, we're gonna walk through all the tables” (OCR: “Database Walkthrough”).

stop_or_escalate_if: If you cannot find the “Database Walkthrough” frame, stop and request the correct segment timestamp/frame set.

steps.title: Follow the presenter’s table-by-table walkthrough and note each table name as it appears
steps.purpose: Create the list of database tables covered by the walkthrough.
steps.instruction: During the walkthrough segment, follow along as the presenter names tables. For each table name that is readable in the available frames, record the table name exactly as it appears.
steps.expected_result: You have a list of the database table names that are readable from the provided walkthrough frames.
steps.healthy_condition: Each recorded table name matches what is visible/readable in the captured frames you are using for the walkthrough.
steps.failure_condition: Table names are not readable in the available frames (e.g., OCR is missing/garbled or the table name text is too low-resolution to confirm).

actions.label: Record readable table names
actions.exact_action: Note each table name as it appears during the walkthrough (only when readable).

stop_or_escalate_if: If table names are not readable from the available frames, stop and request a higher-resolution capture or the next segment that shows the specific table names.

steps.title: Record each table’s walkthrough association/purpose (only what is visible/said)
steps.purpose: Capture the walkthrough’s stated purpose/associations for each table to support later reference.
steps.instruction: For each table you recorded in Step 2, record what the walkthrough associates it with (purpose/what it stores) using only what is visible/said in the available frames. Do not guess beyond what is readable in the frames.
steps.expected_result: For each readable table name, you have a corresponding walkthrough association/purpose statement that is limited to what is visible/readable in the provided frames.
steps.healthy_condition: Each recorded purpose/association is directly supported by the available frame text (e.g., EntityLogs used for logging; Audit tracks AGDID/current geek task ID/command GUID; lattice code model stores lattice codes and station IDs; OPC configuration stores connection parameters; OPC tags stores tags subscribed to on startup).
steps.failure_condition: You cannot determine the purpose/association because the frame text is not readable or the walkthrough explanation is missing from the available captures.

actions.label: Capture purpose/association from readable text
actions.exact_action: Record the walkthrough’s stated purpose/association for each table only when it is visible/readable in the frames.

stop_or_escalate_if: If table names/purpose are not readable from the available frames, stop and request a higher-resolution capture or the next segment that shows the specific table names and explanations.

success_criteria: A list of database table names covered by the “Database Walkthrough” segment is produced from readable frames.
For each recorded table name, a purpose/association statement is captured that is limited to what is visible/readable in the provided frames.
healthy_conditions: Recorded table names and purposes match the readable walkthrough text in the provided artifacts.
No additional tables/purposes are added beyond what is supported by the available frames.
failure_conditions: Table names or purposes cannot be confirmed due to unreadable/low-resolution frames.
Recorded purposes include assumptions not supported by the visible/readable walkthrough text.
escalation_guidance: If table names/purpose are not readable from the available frames, stop and request a higher-resolution capture or the next segment that shows the specific table names and explanations.

screens_or_images.description: Frame containing the walkthrough overview and specific table/model concepts and their stated purposes/associations.
